paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “As requirements for job applications are getting increasingly higher, college students ought to be better prepared for their future career.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“随着工作申请的要求越来越高，大学生应该为未来的职业做好更好的准备。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个长对话。在每次对话结束时，您都会听到四个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 1 至 4 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 5 至 8 基于您刚刚听到的对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear two passages. At the end of each passage, you will hear three or four questions. Both the passage and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将听到两个段落。在每段文章的结尾，你会听到三到四个问题。文章和问题都只会说一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 9 至 11 是基于你刚刚听到的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 12 至 15 题是基于您刚刚听到的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you will hear three recordings of lectures or talks followed by three or four questions. The recordings will be played only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A, B, C and D. Then mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 1 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本部分中，您将听到三段讲座或演讲的录音，然后是三到四个问题。录音只会播放一次。听到问题后，您必须从标有 A、B、C 和 D 的四个选项中选择最佳答案。然后在答题纸 1 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: The slow progress of women in elective office is frustrating for some political observers and experts — including myself. Achieving gender equality in Congress is an important goal. This is because the number of women involved in legislative decisions has significant 26 for all the policies that governments 27 . Female legislators are more likely than men to introduce, speak about and work to pass policies that disproportionately affect women and girls, such as paid family leave, pay 28 and gender-based violence.
paragraphs.translationZh: 女性在民选公职中的缓慢进步令包括我在内的一些政治观察家和专家感到沮丧。在国会实现性别平等是一个重要目标。这是因为参与立法决策的妇女人数对政府制定的所有政策具有重大影响。女性立法者比男性更有可能提出、谈论和努力通过对妇女和女童影响更大的政策，例如带薪家庭假、薪酬公平和性别暴力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Having more women in Congress also fosters a greater sense of connection between female voters and government. In addition, it 29 women’s sense that government cares about their concerns and inspires young women to become more politically engaged.
paragraphs.translationZh: 国会中女性人数的增加还可以增强女性选民与政府之间的联系感。此外，它还增强了妇女的政府关心她们的问题的感觉，并激励年轻女性更多地参与政治。

paragraphs.sourceText: While women are underrepresented in governments around the globe, it is a particularly 30 problem in the United States. Currently, the US ranks 73rd in the world when it comes to female representation in government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管女性在全球政府中的代表性不足，但这在美国是一个尤为严峻的问题。目前，美国在政府中的女性代表性排名世界第 73 位。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the reason women are so 31 underrepresented in US government is not because they face resistance from voters or struggle to raise money. On the contrary, decades of research shows that female candidates raise as much money and win as often as male politicians with similar 32 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 但女性在美国政府中的代表性严重不足的原因并不是因为她们面临选民的抵制或难以筹集资金。相反，数十年的研究表明，女性候选人筹集的资金和获胜的次数与具有类似资历的男性政治家一样多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Rather, the slow progress of women in politics is a tale of two political parties.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相反，女性在政治上的缓慢进步是两个政党的故事。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the next Congress, there will be 107 female Democratic lawmakers and 42 female Republican lawmakers in the Senate and House combined.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在下一届国会中，参众两院将有 107 名女性民主党议员和 42 名共和党女议员。

paragraphs.sourceText: In order for women to gain half of the seats in Congress, more women need to run, 33 on Republican tickets. This will require the Republican Party as a whole to 34 recruiting women — and not just for one election cycle, but in a 35 way.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了让女性在国会获得一半席位，需要更多女性参与竞选，尤其是共和党候选人。这将要求共和党作为一个整体优先考虑招募女性——而且不仅仅是在一个选举周期内，而是以一种持续的方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Benefits of Solitude
paragraphs.translationZh: 独处的好处

paragraphs.sourceText: A) I can be a reluctant socialiser. I’m sometimes secretly pleased when social plans are called off. I get restless a few hours into a hangout. I even once went on a free 10-day silent meditation (冥想) retreat — not for the meditation, but for the silence.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 我可能是一个不情愿的社交者。当社交计划被取消时，我有时会暗自高兴。出去玩几个小时后我会变得焦躁不安。我什至有一次免费参加了为期 10 天的冥想静修——不是为了冥想，而是为了安静。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) So I can relate to author Anneli Rufus, who wrote in Party of One: The Loners’ Manifesto: “When parents on TV shows punished their kids by ordering them to go to their rooms, I was confused. I loved my room. Being there behind a locked door was a treat. To me a punishment was being ordered to play games with my cousin Louis.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B）所以我可以理解作家安内利·鲁弗斯（Anneli Rufus）的观点，她在《一个人的聚会：孤独者宣言》中写道：“当电视节目中的父母通过命令他们的孩子去自己的房间来惩罚他们时，我很困惑。我喜欢我的房间。待在锁着的门后面是一种享受。对我来说，惩罚就是被命令与我的表弟路易斯一起玩游戏。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) Unsocial tendencies like these are often far from ideal. Abundant research shows the harms of social isolation, considered a serious public health problem in countries that have rapidly ageing populations (though talk of a ‘loneliness epidemic’ may be exaggerated). In the UK, the Royal College of General Practitioners says that loneliness has the same risk level for premature death as diabetes. Strong social connections are important for cognitive functioning, motor function and a smoothly running immune system.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 像这样的不合群的倾向往往很不理想。大量研究表明社会孤立的危害，在人口迅速老龄化的国家中，社会孤立被认为是一个严重的公共卫生问题（尽管“孤独流行病”的说法可能有些夸张）。在英国，皇家全科医生学院表示，孤独与糖尿病具有相同的过早死亡风险水平。牢固的社会联系对于认知功能、运动功能和免疫系统的平稳运行非常重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) This is especially clear from cases of extreme social isolation. Examples of people kept in captivity, children kept isolated in abusive orphanages, and prisoners kept in solitary confinement all show how prolonged solitude can lead to hallucinations (幻觉) and other forms of mental instability.
paragraphs.translationZh: D）这一点从极端社会孤立的案例中尤其明显。被囚禁的人、被隔离在虐待儿童的孤儿院以及被单独监禁的囚犯的例子都表明，长时间的孤独会导致幻觉和其他形式的精神不稳定。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) But these are severe and involuntary cases of aloneness. For those of us who just prefer plenty of alone time, emerging research suggests some good news: there are upsides to being alone — for both our work lives and our emotional well-being.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 但这些都是严重的、非自愿的孤独案例。对于我们这些喜欢独处时间的人来说，新兴研究提出了一些好消息：独处对于我们的工作生活和情感健康都有好处。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Solitude is a time for reflection, for thinking about things more deeply. In a world increasingly focused on speed and competitiveness, solitude is precious and something to be treasured. And there are benefits in learning to love your solitude.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 独处是反思的时间，是更深入思考事物的时间。在一个越来越注重速度和竞争的世界里，孤独是宝贵的，值得珍惜的。学会热爱孤独是有好处的。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) One key benefit of solitude is improved creativity. Gregory Feist, who focuses on the psychology of creativity at California’s San Jose State University, has defined creativity as thinking or activity with two key elements: originality and usefulness. He has found that personality traits commonly associated with creativity are openness (receptiveness to new thoughts and experiences), self-confidence, and autonomy — which may include “a lack of concern for social norms” and “a preference for being alone”. In fact, Feist’s research on both artists and scientists shows that one of the most prominent features of creative folks is their lesser interest in socialising.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 独处的一大好处是提高创造力。加州圣何塞州立大学专注于创造力心理学的格雷戈里·费斯特（Gregory Feist）将创造力定义为具有两个关键要素的思维或活动：原创性和实用性。他发现，通常与创造力相关的人格特质是开放性（接受新思想和新体验）、自信和自主——其中可能包括“不关心社会规范”和“偏好独处”。事实上，费斯特对艺术家和科学家的研究表明，富有创造力的人最显着的特征之一是他们对社交不太感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) One reason for this is that such people are likely to spend sustained time alone working on their craft. Plus, Feist says, many artists “are trying to make sense of their internal world and a lot of internal personal experiences that they’re trying to give expression and meaning to through their art.” Solitude allows for the reflection and observation necessary for that creative process.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 原因之一是这些人可能会花持续的时间独自工作。另外，费斯特说，许多艺术家“正在试图理解他们的内心世界和许多内心的个人经历，他们试图通过他们的艺术表达和意义。”独处可以进行创作过程中必要的反思和观察。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) A recent justification of these ideas came from University at Buffalo psychologist Julie Bowker, who researches social withdrawal. Social withdrawal is usually categorised into three types: shyness caused by fear or anxiety; avoidance, from a dislike of socialising; and unsociability, from a preference for solitude. A paper by Bowker and her colleagues was the first to show that a type of social withdrawal could have a positive effect — they found that creativity was linked specifically to unsociability. They also found that unsociability had no correlation with aggression (shyness and avoidance did). This was significant because while previous research had suggested that unsociability might be harmless, Bowker and colleagues’ paper showed that it could actually be beneficial. Unsociable people are likely to be “having just enough interaction,” Bowker says. “They have a preference for being alone, but they also don’t mind being with others.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 最近对这些想法的论证来自布法罗大学心理学家朱莉·鲍克，她研究社交退缩。社交退缩通常分为三种类型：由于恐惧或焦虑而导致的害羞；回避，因为不喜欢社交；以及由于偏爱独处而导致的不合群。鲍克和她的同事的一篇论文首次表明，某种类型的社交退缩可能会产生积极的影响——他们发现创造力与不合群的性格密切相关。他们还发现，不合群与攻击性没有相关性（害羞和回避却与此相关）。这很重要，因为虽然之前的研究表明不社交可能是无害的，但鲍克和同事的论文表明它实际上可能是有益的。鲍克说，不善交际的人可能“只有足够的互动”。 “他们喜欢独处，但也不介意与他人在一起。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Still, it turns out that solitude is important for more than creativity. It’s commonly believed that leaders need to be sociable. But this depends, among other things, on the personalities of their employees. One 2011 study showed that in branches of a pizza chain where employees were more passive, outgoing bosses were associated with higher profits. But in branches where employees were more active, introverted (内向的) leaders were more effective. One reason for this is that introverted people are less likely to feel threatened by strong personalities and suggestions. They’re also more likely to listen.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 尽管如此，事实证明，孤独比创造力更重要。人们普遍认为领导者需要善于交际。但这除其他外还取决于员工的性格。 2011 年的一项研究表明，在一家披萨连锁店的分店中，员工较为被动，离职的老板与更高的利润相关。但在员工更加活跃的分支机构中，内向的领导者效率更高。原因之一是内向的人不太可能感受到强烈的个性和建议的威胁。他们也更有可能倾听。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Since ancient times, meanwhile, people have been aware of a link between isolation and mental focus. After all, cultures with traditions of religious hermits (隐士) believe that solitude is important for enlightenment. Recent research has given us a better understanding of why. One benefit of unsociability is the brain’s state of active mental rest, which goes hand-in-hand with the stillness of being alone. When another person is present, your brain can’t help but pay some attention. This can be a positive distraction. But it’s still a distraction.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 同时，自古以来，人们就意识到孤立和精神集中之间的联系。毕竟，具有宗教隐士传统的文化认为，孤独对于启蒙很重要。最近的研究让我们更好地理解了其中的原因。不合群的好处之一是大脑处于积极的精神休息状态，这与独处时的宁静是相辅相成的。当另一个人在场时，你的大脑会情不自禁地集中注意力。这可能是一种积极的分散注意力的方法。但这仍然是一种干扰。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Daydreaming in the absence of such distractions activates the brain’s default-mode network. Among other functions, this network helps to consolidate memory and understand others’ emotions. Giving free rein to a wandering mind not only helps with focus in the long term but strengthens your sense of both yourself and others. Paradoxically, therefore, periods of solitude actually help when it comes time to socialise once more. And the occasional absence of focus ultimately helps concentration in the long run.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 在没有此类干扰的情况下做白日梦会激活大脑的默认模式网络。除其他功能外，该网络有助于巩固记忆和理解他人的情绪。放开游离的思维不仅有助于长期集中注意力，还能增强你对自己和他人的认识。因此，矛盾的是，当需要再次社交时，一段时间的独处实际上有所帮助。从长远来看，偶尔的注意力不集中最终有助于集中注意力。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) A more recent advocate of thoughtful and productive solitude is Susan Cain, author of Quiet: The Power of Introverts in a World That Can’t Stop Talking and founder of Quiet Revolution, a company that promotes quiet and introvert-friendly workplaces. “These days, we tend to believe that creativity emerges from a decidedly unreserved socialising process, but in fact it requires sustained attention and deep focus,” she says. “Also, humans are such absorbent social beings that when we surround ourselves with others, we automatically take in their opinions and aesthetics. To truly chart our own path or vision, we have to be willing to isolate ourselves, at least for some period of time.”
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 苏珊·凯恩 (Susan Cain) 最近提倡深思熟虑且富有成效的独处，她是《安静：内向者在一个无法停止说话的世界中的力量》一书的作者，也是安静革命的创始人，该公司致力于提倡安静和内向者友好的工作场所。 “如今，我们倾向于认为创造力是从毫无保留的社交过程中产生的，但事实上它需要持续的关注和深度关注，”她说。 “此外，人类是一种善于吸收的社会生物，当我们周围都是他人时，我们会自动吸收他们的意见和审美。为了真正规划自己的道路或愿景，我们必须愿意孤立自己，至少在一段时间内如此。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N) Still, the line between useful solitude and dangerous isolation can be blurry. “Almost anything can be adaptive and maladaptive, depending on how extreme they get,” Feist says. A disorder has to do with dysfunction. If someone stops caring about people and cuts off all contact, this could point to an irrational neglect of social relations. But creative unsociability is a far cry from this. In fact, Feist says, “there’s a real danger with people who are never alone.” It’s hard to examine one’s own thoughts, feelings and motives, to be self-aware, and fully relaxed unless you have occasional solitude. In addition, introverts tend to have fewer but stronger friendships — which has been linked to greater happiness.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 不过，有用的独处和危险的隔离之间的界限可能很模糊。 “几乎任何事物都可能具有适应性和适应不良性，这取决于它们变得多么极端，”费斯特说。疾病与功能障碍有关。如果某人不再关心他人并切断所有联系，这可能表明对社会关系的非理性忽视。但创造性的不合群与此相去甚远。事实上，费斯特说，“对于那些从不孤单的人来说，确实存在危险。”除非偶尔独处，否则很难审视自己的想法、感受和动机，很难有自我意识，也很难完全放松。此外，内向的人往往拥有较少但更牢固的友谊——这与更大的幸福感有关。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) As with many things, quality reigns over quantity. Nurturing a few solid relationships without feeling the need to constantly populate your life with endless chatting ultimately may be better for you.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 与许多事情一样，质量胜过数量。培养一些牢固的关系，而不需要不断地用无休止的聊天来充实你的生活，最终可能对你更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: P. Thus, if your personality tends toward unsociability, you shouldn’t feel the need to change. Of course, that comes with qualifications. But as long as you have regular social contact, you are choosing solitude rather than being forced into it, you have at least a few good friends and your solitude is good for your well-being or productivity, there’s no point agonising over how to fit a square personality into a round hole.
paragraphs.translationZh: P. 因此，如果你的性格倾向于不合群，你不应该觉得需要改变。当然，这是有资格的。但只要你有定期的社交接触，你是选择独处而不是被迫独处，你至少有几个好朋友，而且你的独处有利于你的幸福或生产力，那么就没有必要苦恼如何将方形性格融入圆形孔中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Lots of research demonstrates that being socially isolated is harmful to the elderly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 大量研究表明，社会孤立对老年人有害。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Being alone enables artists to think and observe, which is a must for their creation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37、独处可以让艺术家思考和观察，这是他们创作的必要条件。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. To one writer, being forced to play with others was a penalty while being kept alone in a room was quite a pleasure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 对一位作家来说，被迫和别人一起玩是一种惩罚，而独自待在一个房间里却是一种乐趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Recent research shows for the first time that there is a specific link between being creative and being unsociable.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 最近的研究首次表明，富有创造力和不善于社交之间存在特定的联系。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. We must be willing to stay alone at least for some time in order to plot our own course.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.我们必须愿意独自呆至少一段时间，以便规划自己的路线。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. According to new research, for people who prefer being alone, solitude can be beneficial to their work lives and
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 根据新的研究，对于喜欢独处的人来说，独处对他们的工作生活和生活有益。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. It may turn out to be better for one to cultivate a few steady relationships than to busy themselves socialising.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 对于一个人来说，培养一些稳定的关系可能比忙于社交更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Allowing your mind to wander freely is conducive to sharpening your focus in the long run.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 从长远来看，让你的思绪自由地走动有利于你集中注意力。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Research conducted on artists and scientists indicates that creative people are less interested in hanging out with others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 对艺术家和科学家进行的研究表明，有创造力的人对与他人交往不太感兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. According to Feist, you will have difficulty knowing yourself if you do not stay alone occasionally.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 根据费斯特的说法，如果你不偶尔独处，你将很难了解自己。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.
paragraphs.translationZh: 模拟器最常用于核电、航空和外科等行业，这些行业的故障会导致灾难性的后果。为了最大限度地发挥模拟学习体验的价值，参与者应立即直接将他们的学习成果应用到组织内的特定干预措施中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn’t resist change, but embraces it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大多数组织都渴望部署重大变革计划，但却发现它们几乎不可能实施。这主要是因为成功的变革需要的不仅仅是愿景，它还需要一支不仅不抵制变革而且拥抱变革的员工队伍。

paragraphs.sourceText: To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了取得成功，组织必须制定一个转型计划，使变革能够在其各个部门和各个层面快速推进。无论高级管理层的承诺程度如何，除非各级关键思想领袖都接受变革，否则这一举措将会枯萎和消亡。为了创造这种广泛的热情，学习型领导者必须让员工了解可能发生的事情，这将使他们能够重新思考他们的思维模式，使他们能够摆脱根深蒂固的范式并拥抱学习的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 允许参与者进入模拟环境为他们提供了体验替代现实的机会，这可以促使他们重新思考他们当前的信念。

paragraphs.sourceText: Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于大多数成年人来说，改变行为并不容易。讲座、培训计划和研讨会可以解释转型的智力要素，但它们很少能有效地了解作为重大变革举措核心的行为方面。此外，在正常工作条件下，管理者很少看到员工发展努力的全部效果。因此，像模拟这样的干预可以刺激变革。

paragraphs.sourceText: An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为一种学习工具，有效的模拟可能比体验更好，因为它加速了时间，压缩了空间，并且与现实不同，它是专门为最大限度地提高参与者的学习而设计的。模拟提供了一种身临其境的学习体验，其中技能、流程和知识都可以以现实无法做到的方式突出显示。在无限、无风险的模型中探索、实验和重复应用新知识的能力使模拟成为最富有成效的学习形式之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare “this is us.” If they don’t, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 精心设计的模拟可以使个人和团体深入了解他们的决策和对业务刺激的直观反应如何影响其他参与者和整个组织。然而，为了获得好处，模拟必须感觉像现实。成功模拟结束后，参与者必须声明“这就是我们”。如果不这样做，他们会将这种体验视为一种游戏，这可能很难应用于工作中，或者更糟糕的是，与日常工作任务无关。为了最大限度地从模拟中获益，参与者应该立即应用从经验中学到的知识，在学习和实践之间建立顺畅的联系。

paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 关于组织的成功变革，我们学到了什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. Unlimited growth is not sustainable and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.
paragraphs.translationZh: GDP 增长并不是衡量一个国家表现如何的良好指标，也不应该成为政府的首要目标。无限增长是不可持续的，经济思维正在转向我们应该以经济模式的可持续性为目标的想法。尽管可持续经济对我们的未来至关重要，但它只是达到目的的手段，而不是目的本身。

paragraphs.sourceText: The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? Don’t different people experience different levels of happiness? Even on the broadest interpretation of “happiness” as prosperity or “life satisfaction”, people want different things.
paragraphs.translationZh: 政府应该关注幸福的想法受到了批评。人们担心如何衡量幸福。幸福难道不是一种转瞬即逝的主观心理状态吗？难道不同的人体验到的幸福程度不一样吗？即使将“幸福”最广泛地解释为繁荣或“生活满意度”，人们想要的东西也不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. A government’s obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity. And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，政府不能把生活满意度强加给公民。但我们的幸福依赖于整个社会的共同努力。政府的义务在于创造促进繁荣的条件。我们有充分的理由认为这些条件存在、在全球范围内适用并且可以通过研究发现。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on “real wealth” for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在最近发表的一篇文章中，哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼建议我们应该关注公民的“实际财富”，这不依赖于 GDP 增长。获取是关键：人们不需要拥有，而是需要获取使他们能够过上美好生活的东西。技术进步和社会行为的变化使我们能够更有效地利用我们已有的资产。关注人们获得更好生活所需的资源可能有助于减少不平等。

paragraphs.sourceText: As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by “happiness” advocates. But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.
paragraphs.translationZh: 就目前而言，这与“幸福”倡导者提出的建议有很多共同之处。但对于政府能够而且应该为公民做的事情来说，它设定的门槛太低了。

paragraphs.sourceText: For example, it’s not clear how a “real wealth” economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. In Western countries, at least — poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation — educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens’ continued productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 例如，目前尚不清楚“真正的财富”经济将如何纠正困扰我们社会的精神疾病流行病。至少在西方国家，心理健康状况不佳对福祉的危害比贫困更大。除了大大改善治疗性心理保健的提供之外，政府可以而且应该采取改善心理健康的预防措施。世界卫生组织建议建立促进社区参与的机构——提供促进心理健康技能的教育计划和干预措施。然而，它充分说明了世界卫生组织认为有必要利用改善心理健康的经济效益来说服各国政府，采取拟议措施的成本是合理的。只要经济是他们的首要任务，政府就只需确保公民的持续生产力即可。

paragraphs.sourceText: To demand that governments set the “happiness” of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.
paragraphs.translationZh: 要求政府将公民的“幸福”作为最高优先事项，就是要求政府将公民视为自己的目的。
